body:
QA review of M1.5 (wad-102), commit a31e4827b2af59add5a51541e28fe019712e44be on sbx/m1.5-compat-run: PASS.

Verified independently (read-only, no checkout/edits):
- Files changed match report: docs/work-plan.md (M1.5 ticked), docs/decisions.md (new entry appended, no history edited), agent-comms/docs/m1.5-compat-check.md (new). No vendor/ edits, no secrets, branch/commit-trailer conventions match repo history.
- Ran `cd agent-comms && uv venv --python 3.12 && uv pip install -e ".[dev]" && pytest -q` myself in an isolated .venv (deleted after): 99 passed, exit 0. The 1 xfail/xpass on test_concurrent_sends_get_gapless_unique_seq[bash-reference] is genuinely flaky across repeated runs on my end too (confirmed by running it 5x) but never fails the suite (non-strict xfail, exit 0 both ways) — this matches the developer's disclosure and predates this commit (not touched in this diff).
- Cross-checked the "live e2e run" claim structurally: confirmed /home/agent/work/bin/handoff (the actual on-PATH handoff in this live factory) is byte-identical to agent-comms/src/acp/handoff_compat.py — i.e. this session's own coordinator/developer messages (messages 0001/0002, run bayto-dev task wad-102) really were produced by the acp shim, not a synthetic harness. I independently ran the reference bash handoff (vendor/wad-sbx-workshop/.../bin/handoff) in an isolated tmp FACTORY_DIR for init/send/claim/read and its JSON schema (message fields/order, state.json shape, claim exit codes 0 then 9) matches the shim's live output field-for-field, modulo ids/timestamps as expected.

One finding (non-blocking, doc-accuracy only): agent-comms/docs/m1.5-compat-check.md states the bash reference's rand() suffix is "10 chars" vs the shim's 6. I traced the actual reference script: rand() uses `head -c 6` but the script also has `set -euo pipefail` at the top, so head's early pipe close SIGPIPEs the upstream `tr`, pipefail treats that as a pipeline failure, and the `|| printf '%s' "$$"` fallback fires *in addition to* (not instead of) the 6 chars already written — so real suffixes are "6 random chars + the shell PID" (I reproduced this reliably), a variable length (I saw 11 chars, not a fixed 10). Doesn't change the pass/fail conclusion since message_id is normalized out of the diff either way, but the doc's specific numeric claim there is wrong and wasn't actually re-verified — worth a follow-up correction, not a re-open of M1.5.

Conclusion: acceptance criteria met (real e2e run, not just unit tests, with evidence), AGENTS.md rules followed, work-plan tick is justified. Recommend M1.5 stays ticked.
